searchText: for the `BeaconBlocks` response, which using ssz-encoding returns a vector of blocks, how is the length of the vector determined? or how are others doing it? The spec says to only return blocks if they exist for the requested slots, so the length of the vector in the response isn't able to be determined solely from the request. <@534934855113506836> for blocks that dont exist, we return a ssz null object in its place so the response is a vector of Union[null, BeaconBlock] ? or is that a zeroed out BeaconBlock? It would be the first case, the size of the vector doesnt change from the request ok, thanks Its not a union type. Its is just missing. The type is an SSZ List rather than Vector. The max length of the list is `SSZ_MAX_LIST_SIZE` See the "encoding strategies" in the spec (sorry no link. On mobile) ok, I'll put in a pr to change/remove this line `*Note*: Parameters defined as `[]VariableName` are SSZ-encoded containerless vectors.` <@498009160982724610> <@449019668296892420> i think we need to define interop values for some if the network configuration constants before next week (`REQ_RESP_MAX_SIZE`, `SSZ_MAX_LIST_SIZE`, etc). Will take a look when back on computer That looks like it is in error. The beaconblocks request is a List. The recentbeaconblocks is a known length so could be a vector but also could for consistency just be a list. There isnt really a major gain in specifying as vector here So yeah, PR would be great

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:
Its not a union type. Its is just missing. The type is an SSZ List rather than Vector. The max length of the list is `SSZ_MAX_LIST_SIZE`

See the "encoding strategies" in the spec (sorry no link. On mobile)
